acv.quote: The account was worth about three hundred and twenty K a year.

data.reason: Only the international half of the account was decided, and it moved to local acquiring with Adyen. Adyen tested a slice of the customer's own international traffic and showed results by country, while we answered with average uplift. Our own market-by-market analysis arrived three weeks late, after the test had finished. Elena says it was decided before we got in the room and there was nothing to do, but the evidence shows a late answer and no contact with the new buyer.

trigger.finding: A newly hired head of payments, the company's first, pulled declines by country and saw weak international markets. The rep didn't know he had been hired. This suggests our message should reach new payments leaders early, when they first audit declines by market.
trigger.quote: the first thing he did was pull declines by country. A few of their international markets looked bad to him.

decider.finding: Stefan, the new head of payments, recommended the move and the CFO approved it, as Stefan told Elena on their last call. Our original buyer, the engineering manager, had left, and Elena had never met Stefan before the renewal. The decision reached the CFO two weeks before that last call. So Stefan was the decider, not a champion we had built.
decider.quote: this went to the CFO two weeks ago.

competitor.finding: Stefan said Adyen ran a test on part of their international traffic and returned results by country, and he kept using the phrase 'local acquiring'. Elena doesn't know what the test showed. After that, his questions turned to approval rates by country, card type and issuer, and why. This suggests our answers need to work at that level of detail.
competitor.quote: What's our approval rate in this country, on this card type, by issuer. And why.

message.finding: The Authorization Boost average uplift got silence, then pushback from Stefan, who wanted his own number. He also turned down a roadmap session. In this deal, general uplift claims did not work on a buyer who had to defend his own figures to a CFO.
message.quote: I can't take an average to my CFO.

proof.finding: He asked for a view of his own approval rates by market, with reasons. We delivered it three weeks later, after the Adyen test had finished, and he called it the most useful thing we had sent. He also asked for a named person who reviews his numbers every month, and we had none. This suggests account-specific analysis and a named owner are proof we can offer, if we offer them in time.
proof.quote: He asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month, and I didn't have a name.

words.finding: Stefan called the problem 'money left on the table'. He said 'approvals', not 'authorization', and talked about 'local cards, local rails' and 'what's mine'. Our language was product names and average uplift. This suggests our messaging could use his money-and-markets terms rather than feature names.
